dict.string: Paste plain text with repeated blank lines removed, then restore the original clipboard.

# Clean Paste
Independent Alfred 5 workflow. Default hotkey: **Command + Shift + V**. Alfred Clipboard History now uses Control + Command + V on this Mac. Existing workflows and Alfred preferences are not edited by this package.
## Installation and hotkey
Double-click `Alfred-Clean-Paste.alfredworkflow`, then choose Import in Alfred. If Clean Paste is already installed, use the installed copy rather than importing another copy. In Alfred Preferences > Workflows > Clean Paste, double-click the Hotkey object to inspect or change its shortcut. Alfred can omit assigned hotkeys from exported workflows; if the imported Hotkey field is empty, enter Command + Shift + V there.
The installed Alfred files report version 5.7.3 (2320). A Powerpack license file and existing workflows are present, but license validity and live workflow access must be confirmed in Alfred Preferences. The current automation session could not open Alfred Preferences (Launch Services error -10827), so GUI activation and hotkey registration have not been verified.
The current Alfred configuration assigns Command + Shift + V to Clean Paste and Control + Command + V to Clipboard History. No other configured Alfred workflow or enabled macOS symbolic shortcut matches Command + Shift + V. Live hotkey registration and application-specific shortcuts remain unverified.
## Operation
Copy text, focus an editable field, and press Command + Shift + V. Wait about 1.5 seconds before invoking it again.
The native Hotkey trigger runs `/usr/bin/osascript` in JavaScript for Automation (JXA) mode. AppKit reads explicitly available plain text and snapshots every clipboard item and representation in memory. No clipboard backup is written to disk. The script normalizes CRLF to LF, removes spaces and tabs on otherwise empty lines, and compresses repeated LF to one LF. It preserves indentation, ordinary body spaces, punctuation, Unicode, and a single final newline. It does not expand Alfred placeholders, shell expressions, or text as executable code.
System Events sends Command + V after the clipboard contains only UTF-8 plain text. The original representations are restored after 1.5 seconds if the pasteboard change counter still identifies this workflow's write. A native NSMutableArray retains the backup items without JavaScript array conversion. After restoration, item counts, format counts, and every format's bytes are compared with the backup before success is logged. A new copy during that interval is left intact. Empty, whitespace-only, unsupported, or unreadable clipboard data exits before changing the clipboard. Snapshot and permission failures also exit before changing it.
Run Script is used instead of Replace and Copy to Clipboard because the same process can keep the complete original clipboard in memory and restore it without editing Alfred's global clipboard preferences or writing a backup file.
## Permissions
Alfred must be allowed under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility. The first execution may request Automation access for Alfred/osascript to control System Events. If needed, inspect Privacy & Security > Automation > Alfred > System Events. Grant permissions yourself only if you want this behavior. This workflow does not change permissions, require Full Disk Access, or install Python, Perl, or another runtime. Diagnostics go to the Alfred debugger, never into the target field.
## Clipboard restoration limits and fallback
Restoration is best effort: macOS does not acknowledge when an arbitrary app has finished reading a pasteboard. Slow apps may require increasing `delay(1.5)` in `clean-paste.js` to `delay(3)`. A force-quit, process crash, failed pasteboard write, or clipboard-manager intervention can prevent restoration. Clipboard history tools may observe the temporary clean text; their settings are unchanged.
If an app reliably reads the clipboard too late, the reliable fallback for that app is to leave the cleaned text on the clipboard: edit a separate copy of this workflow and remove the `restoreIfOwned();` call in the `finally` block. That copy will intentionally replace the clipboard with plain text; preserve the source text separately first. Keep the installed default workflow for apps where the restoring behavior works. Secure fields or apps that reject simulated paste may not accept this workflow.
## Verification
Run without touching the clipboard:
```sh /usr/bin/osascript -l JavaScript ./clean-paste.js --self-test ```
All 12 text cases passed in the actual JXA regular-expression engine, including the requested Chinese paragraphs, multiple empty rows, unchanged single LF, mixed English/Chinese with spaces, whitespace rows with CRLF, empty input, Unicode, indentation, a trailing LF, and literal placeholder text.
Real clipboard access in the execution session was unavailable: `pbpaste` returned exit 1, and AppKit exposed no usable clipboard change counter/items. Calling the workflow script exits safely; diagnostic logging now reports `Clean Paste: clipboard service unavailable.` This verifies the unavailable-clipboard guard only. Real empty/image-only clipboard behavior, full-format restoration remains unverified in this tool session. The user has confirmed successful Word paste, and debugger output confirms hotkey dispatch and the paste command. A restoration bridge error was subsequently fixed; final live restoration verification is still pending.
For a manual acceptance check, copy `one`, a blank line, and `two`; focus a new scratch document and invoke the hotkey. Expect two adjacent text lines. After two seconds, ordinary Command + V should paste the original text with its blank line. Also check an empty clipboard and a copied image: nothing should be pasted or replaced. Test in a scratch document, never a shell command prompt.
## Modify, disable, uninstall
Use Alfred Preferences > Workflows > Clean Paste. Double-click Hotkey to change the shortcut; use Open in Finder to inspect the source. Disable the workflow via its context menu, or clear its Hotkey field. Delete only Clean Paste from Alfred to uninstall. This workflow has no persistent data, background service, or other preferences to remove. The archive in Downloads can be retained or deleted.
## Troubleshooting a silent hotkey
Select Clean Paste in Alfred Preferences > Workflows and click the debugger (bug icon). Keep the debugger open, focus a scratch Word document, and invoke Command + Shift + V. Inspect the Run Script messages. `started` confirms that the script ran. Later messages identify a clipboard, snapshot, permission, or focus failure. Only stage names and error numbers are logged; clipboard text is never logged. `paste command sent` confirms dispatch, not acceptance by Word.
The successful restoration diagnostic is now: `Clean Paste: original clipboard restored and verified.` A failed or interrupted verification never logs restoration success.
